authored_explainer.title: Cereal production Is 1.5x Higher Than In 1972
authored_explainer.hook: By the 1970s, experts were warning the world would run out of food.
says: In 1985, progression to secondary school (%) was 77.8; by 2017, 91.3—1.2 times higher.
In 1972, cereal production was 1083.7 million metric tons; by 2024, 1644.1—1.5 times higher.
China leads: 5.2; United States: 4.2; Australia: 3.6; Brazil: 2.4; Russia: 2.2 million square kilometers.
authored_explainer.closing: The famine everyone predicted never showed up.
authored_explainer.question: Which surprised you most—school, grain, or land?

authored_explainer.title: Combustible renewables and waste Is 3.0x Higher Than In 1990
authored_explainer.hook: One energy source has tripled since 1990; it isn't solar or wind.
says: In 1990, combustible renewables and waste was 10.2 %; by 2024, 30.1 %—3.0 times higher.
In 1998, electricity access was 73.2 %; by 2024, 91.9 %—1.3 times higher.
In 1972, methane (ch4) waste emissions were 903.8 Mt CO2e; by 2024, 1,652—1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: A third of the world's energy now comes from waste.
authored_explainer.question: Which surprised you most—fuel, power, or waste?

authored_explainer.title: Population growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth was supposed to accelerate forever; the number proves it didn't.
says: In 1972, rural population was 63.1 %; by 2025, 42.2 %—67 percent of that.
In 1972, largest-city population was 18.2 %; by 2025, 16.2 %—barely moved.
In 1972, population growth was 2 annual %; by 2025, 0.91 annual %—46 percent.
authored_explainer.closing: The planet is still growing; it has almost stopped accelerating.
authored_explainer.question: Which surprised you most—rural, city, or growth?
